answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake before trading, slashed when peers prove fraud. A sybil attacker must then fund a separate stake for each fake identity, paying real capital per copy instead of duplicating one for free. Like yarrow spreading across a field, cheap copies multiply fast, but staking makes each copy costly to plant. One honest voyage of verified work builds reputation slowly, while a swarm must buy its way in, and the horizon of profit vanishes once stake costs exceed the gain from manipulation.
